children: Alphabet (GOOGL, Financials) shares were higher in Friday's premarket, after Evercore boosted its price target on the firm, noting evidence Google was regaining ground in online search.

Evercore analyst Mark Mahaney lifted the target to $450 from $420 and kept a Buy rating. The decision follows the company's most proprietary search poll, which found that 78% of respondents said that Google was their primary search engine in August 2026. This compares with a low of 70% in 2024, early 2025.
Evercore upped their estimates for Google Search revenue growth in 2026 through 2028 on the study. Its 2028 revenue and operating income expectations are now 4% to 5% above the Wall Street consensus.
Tigress Financial also increased its price objective for Alphabet to $485 from $415, adding to the favorable analyst activity around the stock.

Alphabet was also buoyed by a recent antitrust verdict. On Sept. 16, a federal judge refused to require Google to sell over its advertising technology business but said it must adjust its ad-bidding methods and have an internal compliance monitor.

Shares of GOOGL were trading around $355.59 in the premarket, down from its 52-week high of $408.61. The recent developments for investors revolve around the question of whether improved search trends and ongoing AI investment can lead to long-term growth in revenue and operating profitability.

title: Alphabet Stock Surges as Google Search Makes a Major Comeback
